ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (52) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

The opening keeps Tolstoy's play on «тщеславие» (tshcheslaviye, 'vanity') and «тщетный» (tshchetny, 'vain, futile') with 'vain' and 'vanity'. The proverb is printed «Себя уморишь, а людей не увидишь» (Sebya umorish', a lyudey ne uvidish', 'you will wear yourself to death but will not see people'); it is translated as the known proverb with «удивишь» (udivish', 'you will impress'), and the reading is flagged. Attributions follow the print: Penn, Pope, Lichtenberg, La Bruyère, and the bare initial K.

Source observation: [11] «людей не увидишь» ('you will not see people') looks like a transposition of «не удивишь» ('you will not impress'), the known form of the proverb «Себя уморишь, а людей не удивишь»; translated as «удивишь».
